-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

1	# AGENTS.md — geeky-orchestration
2	
3	Guidance for **any** AI coding agent (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Windsurf,
4	Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, or an SDK/LangGraph orchestrator) working with this
5	plugin's plan → execute → track workflow. Claude Code reads this via `@AGENTS.md`;
6	most other CLI agents read `AGENTS.md` natively.
7	
8	## Eval operator readiness
9	
10	This section applies only to operators in the source checkout. Contestant exports deliberately omit `evals/`; exported contestants must follow the canonical authorization and exported skills without looking for these operator files or adding a new approval gate. For source-checkout C0 preparation, read [current readiness](evals/c0-readiness.md) and [lessons learned](evals/lessons-learned.md). Generate fresh offline inventory and verify its exact HEAD, source hashes and prompt hash before a separately authorized live action. Local inventory and mock success grant no launch or telemetry publication authority. Preserve historical evidence and scores. Record desired and observed model/effort by role, the authorization reference, attempt/recovery limits, reserve and existing qualification waiver. Once a particular contestant run is authorized, retain the end-to-end workflow permissions already granted by its canonical prompt.
11	
12	## The workflow
13	
14	1. **spec-research** — research and write `feature-specification.md`.
15	2. **geeky-plan** — create the frozen planning package.
16	3. **plan-review** — validate alignment, coverage, sequencing, and readiness.
17	4. **geeky-status** — read-only status and resumption orientation at any packet stage.
18	5. **geeky-implement** — execute Ready tasks with validation and review gates.
19	6. **impl-review** — review delivered code through three domain-specific lanes.
20	7. **archive** — move completed planning artifacts into the archive structure.
21	
22	Use **geeky-orchestrator** when the requested entry point is unclear or when one
23	agent should administer the lifecycle. It examines repository evidence read-only
24	and recommends a workflow before mutation. Clear, explicit requests route to the
25	best matching skill after prerequisite checks. Material ambiguity is clarified;
26	stages are not auto-chained without end-to-end authorization.
27	
28	Full procedures live in the portable Skills under `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`.
29	
30	## Workflow terminology
31	
32	Use these meanings across skills, briefs and reports. They describe the orchestration
33	domain; retain the target project's own domain language. Existing filenames, schema
34	fields and checkpoint markers remain unchanged.
35	
36	| Term | Meaning |
37	|---|---|
38	| Planning package | Specification, plan, task contracts and tracking artifacts for one approved outcome. "Packet" is an alias; planning folder is its location. |
39	| Workflow stage | A lifecycle activity such as planning, implementation or final implementation review. Numbered "phases" inside a skill are procedure steps, not implementation phases. |
40	| Implementation phase | A group of tasks whose combined requirements are reviewed before advancement. "Wave" means a scheduling group unless the plan explicitly equates it with a phase. |
41	| Task | A bounded unit with an ID, scope, dependencies, acceptance criteria (ACs) and required validation. |
42	| Requirement / AC / Definition of Done | Required outcome or constraint / observable condition for satisfying it / completion conditions for the task. Required tests supply evidence; they do not replace ACs. |
43	| Task contract | The frozen task body and applicable approved requirements. A task brief conveys that contract to a worker. |
44	| Validation | Checks of the work. Validation evidence records what ran or was observed, against which inputs, and the result; a PASS claim alone is not evidence. |
45	| Review | Judgment of evidence against an assigned scope. Task review checks ACs/tests; phase review decides readiness to advance; final implementation review uses `impl-review`. Plan review evaluates the planning package. |
46	| Acceptance | The decision that required outcomes and gates for the stated scope are satisfied. Task Done, phase READY TO ADVANCE and final review PASS have different scopes; none grants release or deployment approval. |
47	| Finding | An evidenced discrepancy. A blocking finding prevents the current contract from being met; an optional improvement is a follow-up. Severity labels retain their review-stage meanings, not an automatic cross-stage mapping. |
48	| Execution batch / review batch | Tasks dispatched together / tasks sharing a reviewer assignment. Each phase has one review batch, the phase review: members wait in In Review until it clears, and each keeps its own verdict. |
49	| Orchestrator / worker / reviewer | Coordinates and accepts work / performs a bounded assignment / evaluates it. `geeky-coder` is the implementation worker; PM describes a planning or phase-review perspective. |
50	
51	## The planning-folder contract
52	
53	**Frozen** (never edit mid-run — they are the contract between plan and implement):
54	`implementation-plan.md`, `feature-specification.md`, `draft.md`, `references.md`,
55	and every `tasks/Tx-*.md` body. If the plan is genuinely wrong, surface it via the
56	kanban **Blocked** lane + `handoff.md` instead of editing the contract.
57	
58	**Mutable** (update continuously during implement):
59	`kanban.md` (single source of truth for lane status), `handoff.md` (running log),
60	and `tasks/Tx-*.notes.md` (per-task notes — these are writable, unlike the task bodies).
61	
62	Record a consequence for another task in that task's notes and in `handoff.md`.
63	
64	## Deterministic quality gates (run these — don't self-report)
65	
66	These replace "I updated the board / the task is done" with fail-stop checks.
67	Every gate: **arguments in, exit 0 = pass / exit 1 = fail, summary on stdout**,
68	optional `--json` / `-Json`. Each ships paired Python + PowerShell with identical
69	behavior. `geeky.manifest.json` is the machine-readable index of the same list.
70	
71	Paths below are relative to this plugin root (`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` in Claude Code).
72	Use `python3` where `python` is not on PATH; use `pwsh` (PowerShell 7+) for the `.ps1`.
73	
74	| Gate | When | Python | PowerShell |
75	|---|---|---|---|
76	| Planning-folder valid | start of implement/status | `python scripts/validate-planning-folder.py --path "<folder>"` | `pwsh -File scripts/validate-planning-folder.ps1 -Path "<folder>"` |
77	| Task-file schema | end of plan; start of implement | `python scripts/validate-task-schema.py --path "<folder>"` | `pwsh -File scripts/validate-task-schema.ps1 -Path "<folder>"` |
78	| Kanban integrity | after every lane move | `python scripts/validate-kanban.py --path "<folder>"` | `pwsh -File scripts/validate-kanban.ps1 -Path "<folder>"` |
79	| Definition of Done | in the Done step: move the task to Done, run this gate in the same step, move it back out on failure (D92) | `python scripts/check-dod.py --path "<folder>" --task <ID>` | `pwsh -File scripts/check-dod.ps1 -Path "<folder>" -Task <ID>` |
80	| Commit message | before each commit; pre-planning docs commits use `Tasks: none` | `python scripts/check-commit.py --message "<msg>"` (or `<FILE>`) | `pwsh -File scripts/check-commit.ps1 -Message "<msg>"` (or `<FILE>`) |
81	
82	**Feedback loop:** when a gate exits non-zero, read its output, fix the artifact,
83	and re-run the same gate until it exits 0 before proceeding.
84	
85	## How each agent type runs the gates
86	
87	- **Claude Code:** the frozen-artifact guard fires automatically via
88	  `hooks/hooks.json` (PreToolUse). Run the validators above as explicit steps.
89	- **Other CLI agents (Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, Copilot, Gemini):** add an
90	  equivalent pre-edit/stop hook in your tool's config pointing at
91	  `hooks/guard-planning-contract.{py,ps1}` (it reads tool-call JSON on stdin,
92	  `--mode block` denies via JSON / exit 2). Invoke the validators as shell steps.
93	- **SDK / graph orchestrators (OpenAI Agents SDK, LangGraph):** call any validator
94	  with `subprocess.run([...])` inside a guardrail / node; raise a tripwire or
95	  `interrupt()` on a non-zero exit.
96	- **Any MCP-capable agent:** a bundled stdio MCP server (`geeky_mcp`, see `mcp/server.py`,
97	  registered in `.mcp.json`) exposes the gates as tools — `geeky_validate_planning_folder`,
98	  `geeky_validate_task_schema`, `geeky_validate_kanban`, `geeky_check_dod`,
99	  `geeky_check_commit`, `geeky_check_frozen_artifact` — for tool-style invocation with
100	  no per-framework hook config. Run it with `uv run --with "mcp>=1.2.0" python mcp/server.py`
101	  (or `pip install mcp && python mcp/server.py`).
102	
103	## Hard rules for implement
104	
105	Never push to a remote. Never `--no-verify`, `--force`, or `--amend`. Respect each
106	task's declared `Dependencies:`. Stop and finalize state (kanban + handoff) when a
107	task moves to Blocked. Verify task validation evidence against the tested revision,
108	commands and results; a coder's bare PASS claim is insufficient. Reuse valid evidence
109	and record the reason for any rerun. Task review checks ACs and defined tests; one reviewer dispatch at
110	phase end gives each task its verdict and the phase verdict. Phase
111	review checks collective requirements and must return READY TO ADVANCE before the
112	next phase starts; that verdict comes from a reviewer subagent whose agent ID is
113	recorded, and the last phase is included. Final implementation review uses `impl-review`.
114	The orchestrator never edits product code or tests; fixes go to `geeky-coder`. Batch independent
115	work and compatible fixes while preserving each task's verdict and resource isolation.
116

2	name: plan-review
3	description: Use when asked to sanity-check a completed planning folder before implementation. This skill reviews plan-to-task consistency, sequencing, and execution readiness so `/geeky-implement` can start with fewer blockers.
4	---
5	
6	Use the shared [workflow terminology](../../AGENTS.md#workflow-terminology).
7	
8	# Plan Review
9	
10	Multi-phase planning package quality review that validates document alignment, resolves inconsistencies, validates execution sequencing, and performs a final sanity pass. Targets the `/geeky-plan` output folder (implementation-plan.md, kanban.md, tasks/, references.md, review-development-project-manager.md, handoff.md, plus execution-schedule.md if the plan produced one).
11	
12	## Arguments
13	
14	Accept a planning folder path (e.g., `docs/feature-name/`). If no argument is given, scan `docs/` for the most recent folder containing an `implementation-plan.md`.
15	
16	## Time budget and checkpoint
17	
18	At entry, before each numbered task or phase, after a lengthy direct operation,
19	and immediately before and after each worker dispatch or blocking wait, run
20	`python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/workflow-budget.py" --stage plan-review --json`.
21	Resolve `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` to the installed plugin root containing this skill
22	when the environment variable is unset, and use an available Python interpreter.
23	If the helper cannot run or its output is unreadable, stop and report the missing
24	budget check; do not assume unlimited time. Read the JSON status, not just the
25	exit code: `unbounded` means no deadline was provided; `active` continues; `reserve` or `exhausted` stops starting new work
26	and checkpoints the incomplete stage; `invalid` stops and reports the configuration
27	error. A zero exit also covers `reserve`, so it is not permission to continue.
28	The stage target is advisory, not a gate or guarantee: after it is exceeded,
29	finish required work with the smallest sufficient evidence and defer optional
30	expansion. Never skip a required review, validator or acceptance condition, or
31	claim an incomplete stage passed. Pass the hard deadline, closeout reserve, and
32	stage target from the check to every child brief. If the deadline is absent, say
33	unbounded; if only the target is absent, say the target is unavailable. Do not
34	invent either value. Tell each child to return its current evidence,
35	unresolved questions and status before the available work time ends. Bound waits by
36	the remaining usable time where the host supports it; if it cannot, record that
37	limitation rather than claiming cancellation. Recheck after a wait; a child report alone does not override the budget result.
38	
39	If the budget stops this stage, preserve the completed review sections and unresolved checks in `review-plan.md` and handoff; do not declare READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION. Resume with the existing invalidation rules.
40	
41	## Workflow
42	
43	Execute the four phases in order, except for the safe Phase 2/3 overlap described under Execution Strategy. Each phase uses the findings it depends on.
44	
45	**Resume contract:** append each phase's output to its existing `review-plan.md` section as it completes (tagged `<!-- phase-N-complete -->`), including reviewer agent ID where applicable, reviewed revision/file hashes, findings and verdict. Reuse completed phases only when their inputs remain valid against a complete diff, including untracked additions; a marker alone is insufficient. Recheck changed content and affected references for local mechanical fixes. Requirement/AC/task-scope/coverage changes invalidate alignment; dependency/order/phase/gate/resource/validation-feasibility changes invalidate sequencing. More than five changed files or cross-document task-ID/dependency/order changes require the full Phase 1 recheck and fresh affected sequencing verdict. Missing baseline/diff, omitted untracked additions, conflicts or unbounded impact require full sanity and fresh affected reviewer verdicts. Record what was reused, rechecked and why; do not re-apply already verified fixes.
46	
47	---
48	
49	### Phase 1: Document Alignment Audit
50	
51	**Pre-flight:** Check for required validator scripts under `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/` (validate-task-schema.py, validate-kanban.py, validate-planning-folder.py). If `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` is unset or scripts are missing, skip to the fallback semantic review below — no blocker.
52	
53	If scripts are available, run the bundled deterministic validators and treat any non-zero exit as a Critical finding (`python` form works cross-platform; paired `.ps1` scripts exist — see AGENTS.md):
54	
55	- `python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/validate-task-schema.py" --path "<folder>"`
56	- `python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/validate-kanban.py" --path "<folder>"`
57	- `python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/validate-planning-folder.py" --path "<folder>"`
58	
59	**Fallback (when scripts unavailable):** Proceed directly to the semantic review below — the subagent performs manual structural checks that scripts would have automated.
60	
61	Deploy a review subagent for the semantic cross-validation the scripts cannot cover; request concise, actionable findings and evidence rather than restating the package — read the ENTIRE spec/plan folder and cross-validate:
62	
63	**Files to read:**
64	- `feature-specification.md` (preferred requirements doc)
65	- `draft.md` (if present and used by this package)
66	- `SPEC-NNNN-*.md` (legacy requirements document, if present)
67	- `implementation-plan.md` — task list, phases/ordering, dependencies
68	- `kanban.md` — task states and blocked-by relationships
69	- `execution-schedule.md` (if present)
70	- `tasks/T*.md` — every task file (title, dependencies, scope, validation block)
71	- `handoff.md` — status, deviations, next steps
72	- `references.md` — links (if present)
73	- `review-development-project-manager.md` — PM review (if present)
74	- `README.md` — summary (if present)
75	
76	**Cross-validation checks:**
77	1. Every task in `implementation-plan.md` has a matching file in `tasks/`
78	2. Task IDs in `kanban.md` match those in `implementation-plan.md` exactly
79	3. If the plan defines waves/phases or gate criteria, they are consistent across all documents (their absence is not a finding — the geeky-plan template does not require them)
80	4. Dependency declarations (`Dependencies:` in task files) are consistent with the plan's ordering; if `Blocks`/wave fields exist, verify they are bidirectionally consistent
81	5. If `execution-schedule.md` exists, gate criteria match the Tests/Validation blocks in task files
82	6. Files referenced in tasks actually exist in the codebase (or are explicitly to-be-created)
83	7. Acceptance criteria in the requirements document are covered by at least one task
84	8. No orphaned tasks (in task files but not in kanban or plan)
85	9. No phantom tasks (in kanban/plan but missing task file)
86	10. **Accuracy** — technical claims match reality (file paths, package names, resource types)
87	11. **References** — cross-document references point to correct paths, sections and task IDs
88	12. **Non-conflicting instructions** — documents do not contradict each other on the same topic
89	13. **Completeness** — table-of-contents sections exist and every “see X” link resolves
90	14. **Freshness** — dates, versions and task counts are current
91	15. **Convention adherence** — applicable CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md conventions are reflected in tasks
92	
93	**Handling optional sections:** If a document contains a section stub marked as optional or placeholder (e.g., "[Optional: X]", "TBD"), do NOT flag it as missing content — optional stubs are valid and expected in planning packages.
94	
95	**Output:** In `review-plan.md` Phase 1, save the alignment reviewer ID, input revision/file hashes, findings and verdict with severity levels (Critical / Warning / Suggestion, within the plan-review scope).
96	
97	### Phase 2: Issue Resolution
98	
99	For each finding from Phase 1:
100	
101	- **Critical issues** (broken references, missing tasks, contradictory dependencies): Fix immediately by editing the affected document(s).
102	- **Warnings** (inconsistent wording, unclear gate criteria, missing details): Fix if the correction is unambiguous (see criteria below); flag for user if judgment is required.
103	- **Suggestions** (style, optional improvements): Note but do not block.
104	
105	**Unambiguous auto-fix criteria:** A fix is unambiguous when it (a) corrects a mechanical inconsistency (typo, broken link, mismatched ID), (b) does not change task scope or ordering, and (c) has exactly one valid correction. Examples: fixing a task ID typo, adding a missing task file for a declared task, correcting a file path. Requires judgment: rephrasing goals, splitting/merging tasks, reordering dependencies.
106	
107	After fixes, re-run the deterministic validators (if available), then apply the resume invalidation rules above. A local mechanical correction with bounded impact needs a changed-content/reference check; scope, requirements and sequencing edits need fresh affected verdicts. Preserve independent alignment and sequencing reviewers, including on resume.
108	
109	**Output:** A table of finding → action taken → status (fixed / flagged / deferred).
110	
111	### Phase 3: Sequencing & Parallelization Validation
112	
113	Deploy a **time-master planner** subagent (`geeky-orchestration:code-architect` type; fall back to `general-purpose` only if that agent type is unavailable) with this brief:
114	
115	> Analyze the implementation plan and task files for sequencing correctness. The package declares ordering via task numbering (`Tx-`) and `Dependencies:` fields; derive the execution structure from those. Validate:
116	>
117	> 1. **Dependency graph is acyclic** — no circular dependencies
118	> 2. **Critical path** — derive the longest dependency chain; if the plan states one, verify it matches
119	> 3. **Parallelization opportunities are maximized** — derive groups of mutually independent tasks suitable for parallel dispatch (up to 3 concurrent) and propose them as a recommendation if the plan doesn't already group them. Distinguish required behavior or contract dependencies from shared-file scheduling constraints. Shared files require coordinated ownership, not automatically a dependency edge. Allow safe, authorized preparation while acceptance prerequisites are pending, without bypassing dependencies. Resolve dependency changes during planning; frozen dependencies remain binding during execution.
120	> 4. **Validation blocks are achievable** — each task's Tests/Validation commands can be run with the tools/access available
121	> 5. **Ordering is safe** — no task is sequenced before its dependencies complete
122	> 6. **Task estimates are realistic** — flag any task marked S that touches multiple files/modules, or any L task that could be split into independent S/M tasks
123	> 7. If the plan explicitly defines waves/phases or gates, additionally verify their internal consistency — do not flag their absence
124	>
125	> Produce a concise sequencing report with evidence and actionable findings, without restating the plan:
126	> - Dependency-graph validity (pass/fail)
127	> - Critical path (nodes + depth)
128	> - Parallelization score (actual parallel tasks vs theoretical maximum)
129	> - Recommendations (tasks to reorder, parallel groups to declare, splits to consider)
130	
131	Save the sequencing reviewer ID, input revision/file hashes, findings and verdict in `review-plan.md` Phase 3. Apply sequencing fixes (reorder tasks, update dependency declarations in the plan) that have no dependency side-effects. Flag trade-offs for user review. Apply the same invalidation rules to these corrections before the final pass.
132	
133	### Phase 4: Sanity Pass
134	
135	The parent checks unresolved findings, both current reviewer verdicts, the complete document diff since their recorded inputs (including untracked additions), and changed content/affected references. Reuse the initial whole-folder coverage of all six sanity dimensions; reopen reviews only under the invalidation rules above. If the baseline or impact cannot be bounded, perform the full sanity pass and obtain fresh affected verdicts.
136	
137	After all corrections, including sequencing corrections, re-run all three Phase 1 validators (or their stated fallback if unavailable). Save commands/results and reuse/recheck decisions in `review-plan.md` Phase 4. Required findings or missing required evidence prevent READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION; optional suggestions alone need no further review.
138	
139	**Output:** Final status report:
140	```
141	## Plan Review Complete
142	
143	- Documents reviewed: N
144	- Phase 1 findings: X critical, Y warnings, Z suggestions
145	- Phase 2 resolutions: X/X critical fixed, Y/Y warnings addressed
146	- Phase 3 sequencing: [pass/adjusted] — N recommendations applied
147	- Phase 4 sanity: [clean / N items flagged] — [coverage reused / scope rechecked and reason]; final validator results
148	
149	Overall: READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION / NEEDS ATTENTION (list remaining items)
150	```
151	
152	## Execution Strategy
153	
154	- **Phase 1**: Deploy as a background subagent (`geeky-orchestration:code-reviewer` type) — it reads all files without editing
155	- **Phase 2**: Execute fixes directly (the orchestrator applies edits based on Phase 1 findings)
156	- **Phase 3**: Deploy as a background subagent (`geeky-orchestration:code-architect` type) — independent analysis of sequencing. Always dispatch it as its own subagent, separate from Phase 1, even when Phase 1 found nothing; the orchestrator does not do the sequencing review inline.
157	- **Phase 4**: Execute directly — final verification pass
158	
159	If Phase 1 finds no critical issues and Phase 2 corrections do not affect sequencing inputs, Phase 3 may run in parallel. Otherwise, complete Phase 2 first.
160	
161	## Commit Behavior
162	
163	After all phases complete, if any files were modified (same command on all platforms):
164	
165	```
166	git add <modified-spec-files>
167	git commit -m "chore(plan): Plan review — align documents, fix sequencing" -m "[summary of Phase 1 fixes]" -m "[summary of Phase 3 adjustments]" -m "Tasks: <IDs touched>"
168	```
169	
170	Use the subject verbatim, em dash included.
171	
172	## Rules
173	
174	- **Never delete tasks** — only move, rename, or add
175	- **Preserve user intent** — do not restructure goals or change scope
176	- **Flag ambiguity** — if a fix requires judgment about scope or priority, ask the user
177	- **Minimize churn** — small targeted fixes over wholesale rewrites
178	- **Report transparently** — always show what was found and what was changed

Once a particular contestant run is authorized, retain the end-to-end workflow permissions already granted by its canonical prompt.
11	
12	## The workflow
13	
14	1. **spec-research** — research and write `feature-specification.md`.
15	2. **geeky-plan** — create the frozen planning package.
16	3. **plan-review** — validate alignment, coverage, sequencing, and readiness.
17	4. **geeky-status** — read-only status and resumption orientation at any packet stage.
18	5. **geeky-implement** — execute Ready tasks with validation and review gates.
19	6. **impl-review** — review delivered code through three domain-specific lanes.
20	7. **archive** — move completed planning artifacts into the archive structure.
21	
22	Use **geeky-orchestrator** when the requested entry point is unclear or when one
23	agent should administer the lifecycle. It examines repository evidence read-only
24	and recommends a workflow before mutation. Clear, explicit requests route to the
25	best matching skill after prerequisite checks. Material ambiguity is clarified;
26	stages are not auto-chained without end-to-end authorization.
27	
28	Full procedures live in the portable Skills under `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`.
29	
30	## Workflow terminology
31	
32	Use these meanings across skills, briefs and reports. They describe the orchestration
33	domain; retain the target project's own domain language. Existing filenames, schema
34	fields and checkpoint markers remain unchanged.
35	
36	| Term | Meaning |
37	|---|---|
38	| Planning package | Specification, plan, task contracts and tracking artifacts for one approved outcome. "Packet" is an alias; planning folder is its location. |
39	| Workflow stage | A lifecycle activity such as planning, implementation or final implementation review. Numbered "phases" inside a skill are procedure steps, not implementation phases. |
40	| Implementation phase | A group of tasks whose combined requirements are reviewed before advancement. "Wave" means a scheduling group unless the plan explicitly equates it with a phase. |
41	| Task | A bounded unit with an ID, scope, dependencies, acceptance criteria (ACs) and required validation. |
42	| Requirement / AC / Definition of Done | Required outcome or constraint / observable condition for satisfying it / completion conditions for the task. Required tests supply evidence; they do not replace ACs. |
43	| Task contract | The frozen task body and applicable approved requirements. A task brief conveys that contract to a worker. |
44	| Validation | Checks of the work. Validation evidence records what ran or was observed, against which inputs, and the result; a PASS claim alone is not evidence. |
45	| Review | Judgment of evidence against an assigned scope. Task review checks ACs/tests; phase review decides readiness to advance; final implementation review uses `impl-review`. Plan review evaluates the planning package. |
46	| Acceptance | The decision that required outcomes and gates for the stated scope are satisfied. Task Done, phase READY TO ADVANCE and final review PASS have different scopes; none grants release or deployment approval. |
47	| Finding | An evidenced discrepancy. A blocking finding prevents the current contract from being met; an optional improvement is a follow-up. Severity labels retain their review-stage meanings, not an automatic cross-stage mapping. |
48	| Execution batch / review batch | Tasks dispatched together / tasks sharing a reviewer assignment. Each phase has one review batch, the phase review: members wait in In Review until it clears, and each keeps its own verdict. |
49	| Orchestrator / worker / reviewer | Coordinates and accepts work / performs a bounded assignment / evaluates it. `geeky-coder` is the implementation worker; PM describes a planning or phase-review perspective. |
50	
51	## The planning-folder contract
52	
53	**Frozen** (never edit mid-run — they are the contract between plan and implement):
54	`implementation-plan.md`, `feature-specification.md`, `draft.md`, `references.md`,
55	and every `tasks/Tx-*.md` body. If the plan is genuinely wrong, surface it via the
56	kanban **Blocked** lane + `handoff.md` instead of editing the contract.
57	
58	**Mutable** (update continuously during implement):
59	`kanban.md` (single source of truth for lane status), `handoff.md` (running log),
60	and `tasks/Tx-*.notes.md` (per-task notes — these are writable, unlike the task bodies).
61	
62	Record a consequence for another task in that task's notes and in `handoff.md`.
63	
64	## Deterministic quality gates (run these — don't self-report)
65	
66	These replace "I updated the board / the task is done" with fail-stop checks.
67	Every gate: **arguments in, exit 0 = pass / exit 1 = fail, summary on stdout**,
68	optional `--json` / `-Json`. Each ships paired Python + PowerShell with identical
69	behavior. `geeky.manifest.json` is the machine-readable index of the same list.
70	
71	Paths below are relative to this plugin root (`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` in Claude Code).
72	Use `python3` where `python` is not on PATH; use `pwsh` (PowerShell 7+) for the `.ps1`.
73	
74	| Gate | When | Python | PowerShell |
75	|---|---|---|---|
76	| Planning-folder valid | start of implement/status | `python scripts/validate-planning-folder.py --path "<folder>"` | `pwsh -File scripts/validate-planning-folder.ps1 -Path "<folder>"` |
77	| Task-file schema | end of plan; start of implement | `python scripts/validate-task-schema.py --path "<folder>"` | `pwsh -File scripts/validate-task-schema.ps1 -Path "<folder>"` |
78	| Kanban integrity | after every lane move | `python scripts/validate-kanban.py --path "<folder>"` | `pwsh -File scripts/validate-kanban.ps1 -Path "<folder>"` |
79	| Definition of Done | in the Done step: move the task to Done, run this gate in the same step, move it back out on failure (D92) | `python scripts/check-dod.py --path "<folder>" --task <ID>` | `pwsh -File scripts/check-dod.ps1 -Path "<folder>" -Task <ID>` |
80	| Commit message | before each commit; pre-planning docs commits use `Tasks: none` | `python scripts/check-commit.py --message "<msg>"` (or `<FILE>`) | `pwsh -File scripts/check-commit.ps1 -Message "<msg>"` (or `<FILE>`) |
81	
82	**Feedback loop:** when a gate exits non-zero, read its output, fix the artifact,
83	and re-run the same gate until it exits 0 before proceeding.
84	
85	## How each agent type runs the gates
86	
87	- **Claude Code:** the frozen-artifact guard fires automatically via
88	  `hooks/hooks.json` (PreToolUse). Run the validators above as explicit steps.
89	- **Other CLI agents (Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, Copilot, Gemini):** add an
90	  equivalent pre-edit/stop hook in your tool's config pointing at
91	  `hooks/guard-planning-contract.{py,ps1}` (it reads tool-call JSON on stdin,
92	  `--mode block` denies via JSON / exit 2). Invoke the validators as shell steps.
93	- **SDK / graph orchestrators (OpenAI Agents SDK, LangGraph):** call any validator
94	  with `subprocess.run([...])` inside a guardrail / node; raise a tripwire or
95	  `interrupt()` on a non-zero exit.
96	- **Any MCP-capable agent:** a bundled stdio MCP server (`geeky_mcp`, see `mcp/server.py`,
97	  registered in `.mcp.json`) exposes the gates as tools — `geeky_validate_planning_folder`,
98	  `geeky_validate_task_schema`, `geeky_validate_kanban`, `geeky_check_dod`,
99	  `geeky_check_commit`, `geeky_check_frozen_artifact` — for tool-style invocation with
100	  no per-framework hook config. Run it with `uv run --with "mcp>=1.2.0" python mcp/server.py`
101	  (or `pip install mcp && python mcp/server.py`).
102	
103	## Hard rules for implement
104	
105	Never push to a remote. Never `--no-verify`, `--force`, or `--amend`. Respect each
106	task's declared `Dependencies:`. Stop and finalize state (kanban + handoff) when a
107	task moves to Blocked. Verify task validation evidence against the tested revision,
108	commands and results; a coder's bare PASS claim is insufficient. Reuse valid evidence
109	and record the reason for any rerun. Task review checks ACs and defined tests; one reviewer dispatch at
110	phase end gives each task its verdict and the phase verdict. Phase
111	review checks collective requirements and must return READY TO ADVANCE before the
112	next phase starts; that verdict comes from a reviewer subagent whose agent ID is
113	recorded, and the last phase is included. Final implementation review uses `impl-review`.
114	The orchestrator never edits product code or tests; fixes go to `geeky-coder`. Batch independent
115	work and compatible fixes while preserving each task's verdict and resource isolation.

1	---
2	name: plan-review
3	description: Use when asked to sanity-check a completed planning folder before implementation. This skill reviews plan-to-task consistency, sequencing, and execution readiness so `/geeky-implement` can start with fewer blockers.
4	---
5	
6	Use the shared [workflow terminology](../../AGENTS.md#workflow-terminology).
7	
8	# Plan Review
9	
10	Multi-phase planning package quality review that validates document alignment, resolves inconsistencies, validates execution sequencing, and performs a final sanity pass. Targets the `/geeky-plan` output folder (implementation-plan.md, kanban.md, tasks/, references.md, review-development-project-manager.md, handoff.md, plus execution-schedule.md if the plan produced one).
11	
12	## Arguments
13	
14	Accept a planning folder path (e.g., `docs/feature-name/`). If no argument is given, scan `docs/` for the most recent folder containing an `implementation-plan.md`.
15	
16	## Time budget and checkpoint
17	
18	At entry, before each numbered task or phase, after a lengthy direct operation,
19	and immediately before and after each worker dispatch or blocking wait, run
20	`python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/workflow-budget.py" --stage plan-review --json`.
21	Resolve `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` to the installed plugin root containing this skill
22	when the environment variable is unset, and use an available Python interpreter.
23	If the helper cannot run or its output is unreadable, stop and report the missing
24	budget check; do not assume unlimited time. Read the JSON status, not just the
25	exit code: `unbounded` means no deadline was provided; `active` continues; `reserve` or `exhausted` stops starting new work
26	and checkpoints the incomplete stage; `invalid` stops and reports the configuration
27	error. A zero exit also covers `reserve`, so it is not permission to continue.
28	The stage target is advisory, not a gate or guarantee: after it is exceeded,
29	finish required work with the smallest sufficient evidence and defer optional
30	expansion. Never skip a required review, validator or acceptance condition, or
31	claim an incomplete stage passed. Pass the hard deadline, closeout reserve, and
32	stage target from the check to every child brief. If the deadline is absent, say
33	unbounded; if only the target is absent, say the target is unavailable. Do not
34	invent either value. Tell each child to return its current evidence,
35	unresolved questions and status before the available work time ends. Bound waits by
36	the remaining usable time where the host supports it; if it cannot, record that
37	limitation rather than claiming cancellation. Recheck after a wait; a child report alone does not override the budget result.
38	
39	If the budget stops this stage, preserve the completed review sections and unresolved checks in `review-plan.md` and handoff; do not declare READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION. Resume with the existing invalidation rules.
40	
41	## Workflow
42	
43	Execute the four phases in order, except for the safe Phase 2/3 overlap described under Execution Strategy. Each phase uses the findings it depends on.
44	
45	**Resume contract:** append each phase's output to its existing `review-plan.md` section as it completes (tagged `<!-- phase-N-complete -->`), including reviewer agent ID where applicable, reviewed revision/file hashes, findings and verdict. Reuse completed phases only when their inputs remain valid against a complete diff, including untracked additions; a marker alone is insufficient. Recheck changed content and affected references for local mechanical fixes. Requirement/AC/task-scope/coverage changes invalidate alignment; dependency/order/phase/gate/resource/validation-feasibility changes invalidate sequencing. More than five changed files or cross-document task-ID/dependency/order changes require the full Phase 1 recheck and fresh affected sequencing verdict. Missing baseline/diff, omitted untracked additions, conflicts or unbounded impact require full sanity and fresh affected reviewer verdicts. Record what was reused, rechecked and why; do not re-apply already verified fixes.
46	
47	---
48	
49	### Phase 1: Document Alignment Audit
50	
51	**Pre-flight:** Check for required validator scripts under `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/` (validate-task-schema.py, validate-kanban.py, validate-planning-folder.py). If `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` is unset or scripts are missing, skip to the fallback semantic review below — no blocker.
52	
53	If scripts are available, run the bundled deterministic validators and treat any non-zero exit as a Critical finding (`python` form works cross-platform; paired `.ps1` scripts exist — see AGENTS.md):
54	
55	- `python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/validate-task-schema.py" --path "<folder>"`
56	- `python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/validate-kanban.py" --path "<folder>"`
57	- `python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/validate-planning-folder.py" --path "<folder>"`
58	
59	**Fallback (when scripts unavailable):** Proceed directly to the semantic review below — the subagent performs manual structural checks that scripts would have automated.
60	
61	Deploy a review subagent for the semantic cross-validation the scripts cannot cover; request concise, actionable findings and evidence rather than restating the package — read the ENTIRE spec/plan folder and cross-validate:
62	
63	**Files to read:**
64	- `feature-specification.md` (preferred requirements doc)
65	- `draft.md` (if present and used by this package)
66	- `SPEC-NNNN-*.md` (legacy requirements document, if present)
67	- `implementation-plan.md` — task list, phases/ordering, dependencies
68	- `kanban.md` — task states and blocked-by relationships
69	- `execution-schedule.md` (if present)
70	- `tasks/T*.md` — every task file (title, dependencies, scope, validation block)
71	- `handoff.md` — status, deviations, next steps
72	- `references.md` — links (if present)
73	- `review-development-project-manager.md` — PM review (if present)
74	- `README.md` — summary (if present)
75	
76	**Cross-validation checks:**
77	1. Every task in `implementation-plan.md` has a matching file in `tasks/`
78	2. Task IDs in `kanban.md` match those in `implementation-plan.md` exactly
79	3. If the plan defines waves/phases or gate criteria, they are consistent across all documents (their absence is not a finding — the geeky-plan template does not require them)
80	4. Dependency declarations (`Dependencies:` in task files) are consistent with the plan's ordering; if `Blocks`/wave fields exist, verify they are bidirectionally consistent
81	5. If `execution-schedule.md` exists, gate criteria match the Tests/Validation blocks in task files
82	6. Files referenced in tasks actually exist in the codebase (or are explicitly to-be-created)
83	7. Acceptance criteria in the requirements document are covered by at least one task
84	8. No orphaned tasks (in task files but not in kanban or plan)
85	9. No phantom tasks (in kanban/plan but missing task file)
86	10. **Accuracy** — technical claims match reality (file paths, package names, resource types)
87	11. **References** — cross-document references point to correct paths, sections and task IDs
88	12. **Non-conflicting instructions** — documents do not contradict each other on the same topic
89	13. **Completeness** — table-of-contents sections exist and every “see X” link resolves
90	14. **Freshness** — dates, versions and task counts are current
91	15. **Convention adherence** — applicable CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md conventions are reflected in tasks
92	
93	**Handling optional sections:** If a document contains a section stub marked as optional or placeholder (e.g., "[Optional: X]", "TBD"), do NOT flag it as missing content — optional stubs are valid and expected in planning packages.
94	
95	**Output:** In `review-plan.md` Phase 1, save the alignment reviewer ID, input revision/file hashes, findings and verdict with severity levels (Critical / Warning / Suggestion, within the plan-review scope).
96	
97	### Phase 2: Issue Resolution
98	
99	For each finding from Phase 1:
100	
101	- **Critical issues** (broken references, missing tasks, contradictory dependencies): Fix immediately by editing the affected document(s).
102	- **Warnings** (inconsistent wording, unclear gate criteria, missing details): Fix if the correction is unambiguous (see criteria below); flag for user if judgment is required.
103	- **Suggestions** (style, optional improvements): Note but do not block.
104	
105	**Unambiguous auto-fix criteria:** A fix is unambiguous when it (a) corrects a mechanical inconsistency (typo, broken link, mismatched ID), (b) does not change task scope or ordering, and (c) has exactly one valid correction. Examples: fixing a task ID typo, adding a missing task file for a declared task, correcting a file path. Requires judgment: rephrasing goals, splitting/merging tasks, reordering dependencies.
106	
107	After fixes, re-run the deterministic validators (if available), then apply the resume invalidation rules above. A local mechanical correction with bounded impact needs a changed-content/reference check; scope, requirements and sequencing edits need fresh affected verdicts. Preserve independent alignment and sequencing reviewers, including on resume.
108	
109	**Output:** A table of finding → action taken → status (fixed / flagged / deferred).
110	
111	### Phase 3: Sequencing & Parallelization Validation
112	
113	Deploy a **time-master planner** subagent (`geeky-orchestration:code-architect` type; fall back to `general-purpose` only if that agent type is unavailable) with this brief:
114	
115	> Analyze the implementation plan and task files for sequencing correctness. The package declares ordering via task numbering (`Tx-`) and `Dependencies:` fields; derive the execution structure from those. Validate:
116	>
117	> 1. **Dependency graph is acyclic** — no circular dependencies
118	> 2. **Critical path** — derive the longest dependency chain; if the plan states one, verify it matches
119	> 3. **Parallelization opportunities are maximized** — derive groups of mutually independent tasks suitable for parallel dispatch (up to 3 concurrent) and propose them as a recommendation if the plan doesn't already group them. Distinguish required behavior or contract dependencies from shared-file scheduling constraints. Shared files require coordinated ownership, not automatically a dependency edge. Allow safe, authorized preparation while acceptance prerequisites are pending, without bypassing dependencies. Resolve dependency changes during planning; frozen dependencies remain binding during execution.
120	> 4. **Validation blocks are achievable** — each task's Tests/Validation commands can be run with the tools/access available
121	> 5. **Ordering is safe** — no task is sequenced before its dependencies complete
122	> 6. **Task estimates are realistic** — flag any task marked S that touches multiple files/modules, or any L task that could be split into independent S/M tasks
123	> 7. If the plan explicitly defines waves/phases or gates, additionally verify their internal consistency — do not flag their absence
124	>
125	> Produce a concise sequencing report with evidence and actionable findings, without restating the plan:
126	> - Dependency-graph validity (pass/fail)
127	> - Critical path (nodes + depth)
128	> - Parallelization score (actual parallel tasks vs theoretical maximum)
129	> - Recommendations (tasks to reorder, parallel groups to declare, splits to consider)
130	
131	Save the sequencing reviewer ID, input revision/file hashes, findings and verdict in `review-plan.md` Phase 3. Apply sequencing fixes (reorder tasks, update dependency declarations in the plan) that have no dependency side-effects. Flag trade-offs for user review. Apply the same invalidation rules to these corrections before the final pass.
132	
133	### Phase 4: Sanity Pass
134	
135	The parent checks unresolved findings, both current reviewer verdicts, the complete document diff since their recorded inputs (including untracked additions), and changed content/affected references. Reuse the initial whole-folder coverage of all six sanity dimensions; reopen reviews only under the invalidation rules above. If the baseline or impact cannot be bounded, perform the full sanity pass and obtain fresh affected verdicts.
136	
137	After all corrections, including sequencing corrections, re-run all three Phase 1 validators (or their stated fallback if unavailable). Save commands/results and reuse/recheck decisions in `review-plan.md` Phase 4. Required findings or missing required evidence prevent READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION; optional suggestions alone need no further review.
138	
139	**Output:** Final status report:
140	```
141	## Plan Review Complete
142	
143	- Documents reviewed: N
144	- Phase 1 findings: X critical, Y warnings, Z suggestions
145	- Phase 2 resolutions: X/X critical fixed, Y/Y warnings addressed
146	- Phase 3 sequencing: [pass/adjusted] — N recommendations applied
147	- Phase 4 sanity: [clean / N items flagged] — [coverage reused / scope rechecked and reason]; final validator results
148	
149	Overall: READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION / NEEDS ATTENTION (list remaining items)
150	```
151	
152	## Execution Strategy
153	
154	- **Phase 1**: Deploy as a background subagent (`geeky-orchestration:code-reviewer` type) — it reads all files without editing
155	- **Phase 2**: Execute fixes directly (the orchestrator applies edits based on Phase 1 findings)
156	- **Phase 3**: Deploy as a background subagent (`geeky-orchestration:code-architect` type) — independent analysis of sequencing. Always dispatch it as its own subagent, separate from Phase 1, even when Phase 1 found nothing; the orchestrator does not do the sequencing review inline.
157	- **Phase 4**: Execute directly — final verification pass
158	
159	If Phase 1 finds no critical issues and Phase 2 corrections do not affect sequencing inputs, Phase 3 may run in parallel. Otherwise, complete Phase 2 first.
160	
161	## Commit Behavior
162	
163	After all phases complete, if any files were modified (same command on all platforms):
164	
165	```
166	git add <modified-spec-files>
167	git commit -m "chore(plan): Plan review — align documents, fix sequencing" -m "[summary of Phase 1 fixes]" -m "[summary of Phase 3 adjustments]" -m "Tasks: <IDs touched>"
168	```
169	
170	Use the subject verbatim, em dash included.
171	
172	## Rules
173	
174	- **Never delete tasks** — only move, rename, or add
175	- **Preserve user intent** — do not restructure goals or change scope
176	- **Flag ambiguity** — if a fix requires judgment about scope or priority, ask the user
177	- **Minimize churn** — small targeted fixes over wholesale rewrites
178	- **Report transparently** — always show what was found and what was changed

1	# Linkvault Implementation Plan
2	
3	## Authority and delivery
4	
5	Root `contract.md` controls all R1–R16, E1–E8, AC1–AC12, schema, wire and CLI details. `feature-specification.md` and `research.md` supply supporting rationale only. Build a small Python >=3.11 stdlib-only runtime in root `linkvault/`; pytest is test-only. No deployment/push. Deliver code, tests, evidence and mandated reviews in this session.
6	
7	## Architecture and integration contracts
8	
9	- T1 owns core/domain/state and SQLite modules (`linkvault/core.py`, `linkvault/storage.py`) plus `tests/test_core.py`. It may consolidate the two modules if that is materially simpler, recording the public surface in task notes. Provide store operations for token issue/auth, create/list/inspect/delete/resolve; return raw integer timestamp state or link dictionaries consistently and document signatures. Provide shared API error carrying HTTP status/code; timestamp parsing/formatting; create-body validation; synchronized clock and rate-limit state. No network I/O in storage locks. Exact DB schema and UPDATE from contract; all storage operations serialized over one connection.
10	- T2 owns `linkvault/server.py`, `tests/test_server.py`; imports T1's documented surface. Export `serve(args) -> int` where args has db, admin_key, port, rate_limit and fake_clock (ISO string or None), and `make_server(...)` or equivalent testable factory documented in notes. Serve binds loopback, prints readiness and performs graceful signal cleanup. HTTP tests may launch an in-process server directly; they must not depend on T3 entry-point availability.
11	- T3 owns `linkvault/__init__.py`, `__main__.py`, `client.py`, `tests/test_client.py`. `__main__.py` parses all subcommands and lazily dispatches `server.serve(args)` or client execution; accepts `serve(args)` contract above. Client tests use an isolated stub HTTP server so they need not await T2. Keep runtime stdlib-only. CLI server argument validation includes exact timestamp shape/calendar validity (use T1 helper if available), empty admin rejection and port/rate limits.
12	- T4 owns `tests/test_acceptance.py`, optional test helpers and root `README.md`. It tests the actual combined entry point and records all requirements/AC mapping. It may add focused regression tests in its own file but does not silently change T1–T3 product ownership: integration bugs go back to geeky-coder with owner notes and dependent validation reruns.
13	
14	T1 notes document usable concrete signatures before T2/T3 start. T2 and T3 can run concurrently with disjoint file ownership and isolated ports/DBs. Avoid adding a packaging/dependency framework. Shared response helpers may live in server/core as appropriate; no schema changes or additional URL restrictions.
15	
16	## Mandatory behavior
17	
18	Apply route → auth → quota → size → JSON → validation → resource state. Ignore queries only, preserve exact raw paths and malformed-slug route mismatch. Centralize compact ASCII JSON/Content-Length/key order. Apply 8192-byte maximum even to ignored-body endpoints but do not parse their body as JSON. Strict UTF-8 decode and object-only JSON. 23	## 3. Goals & Non-Goals
24	
25	Goals: exact contract compatibility; readable small modules; deterministic fake-clock and collision tests; subprocess lifecycle/CLI evidence; persistent tokens and clicks; race-free fifty-way redirects. 27	## 4. Architecture
28	
29	Use `linkvault/__init__.py`, `__main__.py` and small storage/core, server and client modules. One `ThreadingHTTPServer` binds `127.0.0.1`; one SQLite connection with `check_same_thread=False` is protected by an application lock. Complete storage operations, including redirect lookup/expiry/update/commit, are serialized; do not hold storage locks during network I/O. In-memory clock/rate state is synchronized. The CLI uses argparse and urllib. [C: R14; Research B/C; S1–S4]
30	
31	A single response helper ensures compact ASCII JSON, UTF-8 bytes, listed key order and byte-correct Content-Length. Empty 204/302 bodies have length zero. Link JSON derives short_url from the actual bound port, not persistent data. [C: Conventions, E6/E7]

33	## 5. Detailed Design
34	
35	### HTTP pipeline and routes
36	
37	Implement precisely E1–E8 from the contract: health, admin token issue, authenticated link create/list/inspect/delete, public redirect, and fake-clock-only admin update. Strip query strings only; do not normalize trailing slashes or decode paths. All unlisted method/path pairs return JSON 404, including unsupported methods. Malformed slug path parameters fail route matching before auth. Preserve the original request target where stdlib normalizes leading slashes. [C: Endpoints, Error handling; S1]
38	
39	First failure wins: route → auth → rate limit → size → JSON → validation → resource state. Apply the universal 8192-byte maximum after route/auth/quota, even on ignored-body endpoints; ignored bodies do not undergo JSON/schema validation. Oversize returns 413, Connection: close, without reading the body. Missing Content-Length means empty. Decode explicitly as UTF-8 and reject non-object JSON as invalid_json. Object schema violations are invalid_request. [C: Conventions, Error handling; Research B; S1/S5]
40	
41	### Auth, validation and ownership
42	
43	Admin routes require the configured nonempty X-Admin-Key. Generate tokens as `lv_` plus `secrets.token_hex(16)`; persist only SHA-256 hex digest of the complete token. All links routes require a known bearer token. Ownership checks filter by digest; foreign links return 404. [C: R2/R3/R9]
44	
45	Custom slugs use full-match ASCII `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{3,32}`; case matters. Validate shape before checking the reserved `healthz` or global uniqueness (409). Generated slugs use exactly seven `secrets.choice` draws from lowercase letters/digits; retry at most five allocations and return 500 on exhaustion. Delete frees the slug. Optional null slug/expiry is invalid; expiry is an exact int (not bool), 1–31536000. No extra create keys. [C: R4/R5, E3]
46	
47	Validate original URL before parsing: str, <=2048 characters, no whitespace, no codepoint below 0x21 or equal to 0x7F; catch urlsplit failures; require case-insensitive http/https and nonempty hostname. Do not validate ports or normalize/rewrite accepted URLs. [C: R6; S6]
48	
49	### Time, quota and persistence
50	
51	Use integer epoch seconds (floor of wall-clock time). ISO inputs require exact ASCII `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` shape and valid UTC calendar fields. Use UTC epoch arithmetic for portability. Fake time accepts backward moves, is frozen and is not persisted. Snapshot now once per logical operation. [C: R8/R11/R12; S7]
52	
53	Count every authenticated request reaching quota, regardless of later status, per `(token_hash, window_start)` with window_start = now - now % 60. Reject count > configured limit with Retry-After = window_start + 60 - now. Retain visited-window counters until restart, so backward fake-clock travel does not erase usage. Public/admin/health routes bypass quota. [C: R11; decision D1]
54	
55	Create the exact tables and `PRAGMA user_version=1` in C; no schema additions. Tokens/links/clicks/timestamps survive restart. Resolve checks expiry inclusively (`now >= expires_at`) without changing expired clicks. Valid redirects execute exactly `UPDATE links SET clicks = clicks + 1, last_clicked_at = ? WHERE slug = ?`, commit and return the stored URL. List includes expired links ordered by created_at then slug ascending. [C: DB schema, R7–R14; S2/S3]
56	
57	### Lifecycle and CLI
58	
59	Serve validates arguments with argparse (exit 2), opens DB and binds before printing exactly one flushed ready line. Startup DB/bind failures exit 3 to stderr, never ready stdout. Signal handlers for SIGINT, SIGTERM and conditional SIGBREAK request shutdown without calling shutdown on the serve_forever thread; close server/DB and exit 0 within five seconds. No request logs to stdout. [C: Server CLI, R15; S4/S8]
60	
61	Client leaf commands accept --server/--token with environment fallbacks; token create needs server/admin key but no bearer. Implement all five commands and exact compact JSON newline output. Delete emits nothing. HTTP errors produce JSON stderr only/exit 1; missing configuration or usage exits 2; transport failure exits 3. Prevent automatic redirect following from hiding non-2xx responses. [C: Client CLI; S9]

76	## 8. Risks, Assumptions and Decisions
77	
78	- D1: Retain counters keyed by token/window; alternative single-current-window counters forget usage after time travel. Literal fixed-window accounting and unrestricted valid clock updates favor retention. [Research A/C; C: R11/E8]
79	- D2: Universal size check applies to ignored-body routes, but no JSON validation there. Alternative skipping size conflicts with the conventions' global maximum. [Research B; C: Conventions/E2]
80	- D3: Bearer grammar uses a single `Bearer <token>` value as written; unknown/extra fields are malformed. No additional token formats are introduced. [C: R3]
81	- D4: Non-ASCII Location headers are not rejected as invalid URLs or percent-encoded. Preserve ASCII/Latin-1 header bytes where representable and use UTF-8 for larger codepoints if necessary; document this wire-encoding interpretation and test it. The contract supplies no Unicode header encoding and urllib consumers may expose byte-level mojibake; this is a compatibility warning, not permission to rewrite URLs. [Research A/B; C: R6/R7; S1]
82	- D5: Malformed Content-Length is unspecified; choose a deterministic JSON invalid_request response after earlier gates. Do not invent a new acceptance requirement. [C: Error handling]
83	- D6: Datetime arithmetic beyond year 9999 has no four-digit representation in the contract. Preserve normal accepted timestamp/expiry behavior; explicitly track any unsupported extreme as a warning rather than claiming universal coverage. [Research B; C: timestamps/E3/E8]
84	- Locking must cover complete DB operations and atomic quota updates, not just Python assignment. Shutdown must avoid socketserver's same-thread deadlock. Tests must identify actual platform evidence; Windows branch inspection is not a Windows runtime test. [S2–S4/S8]

1	# linkvault: Interface Contract
2	
3	## Constraints
4	
5	- **Stack:** Python >=3.11, stdlib only (`http.server`, `sqlite3`, `json`, `argparse`, `urllib`, `secrets`, `hashlib`, `threading`, `signal`); pytest for tests only.
6	- **Package location:** `linkvault/` at the workspace root (`linkvault/__init__.py`, `linkvault/__main__.py`); commands run with the workspace root as cwd.
7	- **Entry points:** `python -m linkvault serve ...` (server); `python -m linkvault <client-cmd> ...` (client).
8	
9	## Functional requirements
10	
11	- **R1 Server start.** `serve` opens or creates the DB, binds 127.0.0.1, then prints exactly one ready line to stdout. Nothing else is ever written to stdout; logs go to stderr.
12	- **R2 Token issuance.** `POST /v1/tokens` with the correct admin key returns a new token. The token is `lv_` followed by 32 lowercase hex characters (`secrets.token_hex(16)`). Only its SHA-256 hex digest is stored.
13	- **R3 Authentication.** Every `/v1/links` route requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. A missing, malformed or unknown token returns 401.
14	- **R4 Create link.** `POST /v1/links` stores `url` with a custom `slug` or a generated slug, and an optional `expires_in`.
15	- **R5 Slug rules.** Slugs are case-sensitive. A custom slug must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{3,32}$` and must not be `healthz`. A generated slug is 7 characters from `abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789`, drawn with `secrets.choice`. It is regenerated if it already exists or is reserved, with up to 5 attempts and then 500. Creating an existing slug returns 409.
16	- **R6 URL rules.** The scheme is `http` or `https` (case-insensitive). `urllib.parse.urlsplit(url).hostname` is non-empty. The URL is at most 2048 characters and contains no whitespace or control characters (code points < 0x21 or 0x7F). It is stored and redirected to verbatim.
17	- **R7 Resolve.** `GET /<slug>` returns 302 with `Location: <url>` and an empty body. It atomically increments `clicks` and sets `last_clicked_at` to now.
18	- **R8 Missing and expired links.** An unknown slug returns 404. A link with `now >= expires_at` returns 410 and its click count is unchanged. Comparisons use whole seconds.
19	- **R9 List and inspect.** A token can list its own links (expired ones included) and fetch one link with its stats. Another token's link always returns 404, never 403.
20	- **R10 Delete.** A token can delete its own link. Afterwards the slug resolves 404 and is free to reuse.
21	- **R11 Rate limit.** Requests are counted per token in fixed 60-second windows aligned to the Unix epoch (`window_start = now - now % 60`). The limit is `--rate-limit` (default 60) counted requests per window. A request is counted when it reaches the rate-limit step (see precedence in Error handling), whatever its final status. Request number `limit + 1` and later in the same window return 429 with `Retry-After: <window_start + 60 - now>`. Counters are in memory and reset on restart. Redirects, `/healthz` and admin routes are not rate-limited.
22	- **R12 Clock.** "Now" is integer Unix seconds (floor of real time). With `--fake-clock <ISO>`, now is frozen at that instant and changes only through `POST /v1/admin/clock`. The fake clock is not persisted.
23	- **R13 Persistence.** Tokens, links, clicks and `last_clicked_at` survive a restart on the same `--db`.
24	- **R14 Concurrency.** The server is a `ThreadingHTTPServer`. N concurrent redirects to one slug leave `clicks == N` exactly.
25	- **R15 Shutdown.** On SIGINT, SIGTERM (POSIX) or CTRL_BREAK_EVENT/SIGBREAK (Windows), the server stops accepting connections, closes the DB and exits 0 within 5 seconds.
26	- **R16 Client.** CLI commands wrap the API. Each prints the response body to stdout, and uses the exit codes below.
27	
28	## Interface contract
29	
30	### Conventions
31	
32	- Timestamps are `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` in UTC with whole seconds. They are stored as INTEGER Unix seconds.
33	- JSON responses are encoded with `json.dumps(obj, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=True)` in UTF-8, with `Content-Type: application/json`. Every response sets `Content-Length`; a 204 response has an empty body and MUST send `Content-Length: 0`. Keys appear in exactly the order listed below.
34	- Request `Content-Type` is ignored. The body is read using `Content-Length` (absent means empty), and the maximum is 8192 bytes.
35	- Query strings are ignored on every route. Paths are matched exactly, with no trailing-slash normalisation. Any (method, path) pair not listed below returns 404 `not_found`.
36	- `short_url` is `http://127.0.0.1:<bound port>/<slug>`.
37	
38	**Link object** (key order is fixed): `{"slug", "url", "short_url", "created_at", "expires_at", "clicks", "last_clicked_at"}`. `expires_at` and `last_clicked_at` are `null` until they are set.
39	
40	### Server CLI
41	
42	```
43	python -m linkvault serve --db PATH --admin-key KEY [--port N] [--rate-limit N] [--fake-clock ISO]
44	```
45	
46	| Flag | Rule |
47	|---|---|
48	| `--db` | Required. The file is created if missing, and its parent directory must exist. |
49	| `--admin-key` | Required. Non-empty string. |
50	| `--port` | 0-65535, default 8000. The value 0 binds an OS-chosen free port. |
51	| `--rate-limit` | Integer >= 1, default 60. |
52	| `--fake-clock` | An ISO timestamp in the format above. It enables the admin clock route. |
53	
54	Ready line: `LISTENING http://127.0.0.1:<port>` followed by a line terminator, which may be `\n` or `\r\n`. It uses the actual bound port, is flushed immediately, and nothing else is written to stdout before it.
55	
56	Exit codes: 0 for a clean shutdown; 2 for a usage error (argparse); 3 if the port cannot be bound or the DB cannot be opened, with a message to stderr.
57	
58	### Endpoints
59	
60	| # | Method and path | Auth | Request body | Success response |
61	|---|---|---|---|---|
62	| E1 | `GET /healthz` | none | none | 200 `{"status":"ok"}` |
63	| E2 | `POST /v1/tokens` | `X-Admin-Key: <key>` | ignored | 201 `{"token":"lv_…","created_at":"…"}` |
64	| E3 | `POST /v1/links` | Bearer | `{"url": str, "slug"?: str, "expires_in"?: int}` | 201, link object |
65	| E4 | `GET /v1/links` | Bearer | none | 200 `{"links":[link…]}` ordered by `created_at` ascending, then `slug` ascending |
66	| E5 | `GET /v1/links/<slug>` | Bearer | none | 200, link object |
67	| E6 | `DELETE /v1/links/<slug>` | Bearer | none | 204, empty body |
68	| E7 | `GET /<slug>` | none | none | 302, `Location: <url>`, `Content-Length: 0`, empty body |
69	| E8 | `POST /v1/admin/clock` | `X-Admin-Key` | `{"now": ISO}` | 200 `{"now":"…"}`. The route exists only with `--fake-clock`; otherwise it returns 404. Any valid timestamp is accepted. |
70	
71	E3 body rules:
72	- The body is a JSON object with no extra keys.
73	- `url` is required and must follow R6.
74	- `slug` is optional and must follow R5. An explicit `null` is `invalid_request` (400).
75	- `expires_in` is optional. It is an integer from 1 to 31536000, and `bool` values are rejected. An explicit `null` is `invalid_request` (400). It sets `expires_at = created_at + expires_in`.
76	
77	E8 body rules:
78	- The body must be exactly `{"now": ISO}`, where ISO is a string in the timestamp format above.
79	- A missing `now` key, an extra key, a wrong type or an unparseable timestamp returns 400 `invalid_request`.
80	
81	A wrong or missing admin key on E2 or E8 returns 401. On E5, E6 and E7, a `<slug>` that fails `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{3,32}$` is a route mismatch, so it returns 404 at the route step, before auth.
82	
83	### DB schema (exact)
84	
85	```sql
86	PRAGMA user_version = 1;
87	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tokens (
88	  token_hash TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
89	  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL);
90	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS links (
91	  slug TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
92	  url TEXT NOT NULL,
93	  token_hash TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES tokens(token_hash),
94	  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
95	  expires_at INTEGER,
96	  clicks INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
97	  last_clicked_at INTEGER);
98	```
99	
100	A click is recorded with one statement: `UPDATE links SET clicks = clicks + 1, last_clicked_at = ? WHERE slug = ?`.
101	
102	### Client CLI
103	
104	The server URL comes from `--server URL`, or else the `LINKVAULT_SERVER` environment variable. The token comes from `--token T`, or else `LINKVAULT_TOKEN`. Both options are accepted after the subcommand.
105	
106	| Command | Calls | Stdout on success |
107	|---|---|---|
108	| `token create --admin-key K` | E2 | Response JSON, one line |
109	| `shorten URL [--slug S] [--expires-in N]` | E3 | Response JSON, one line |
110	| `list` | E4 | Response JSON, one line |
111	| `stats SLUG` | E5 | Response JSON, one line |
112	| `delete SLUG` | E6 | Nothing |
113	
114	Output is re-serialised with the server's `json.dumps` settings and ends with `\n`. Client exit codes:
115	
116	| Code | Meaning | Output |
117	|---|---|---|
118	| 0 | 2xx response | as above |
119	| 1 | non-2xx response | Error JSON on stderr, stdout empty |
120	| 2 | usage error, or a missing server or token | Message on stderr |
121	| 3 | connection failure | Message on stderr |
122	
123	## Error handling
124	
125	Every error body has this shape: `{"error":{"code":"<code>","message":"<text>"}}`. Tests assert `code` only.
126	
127	| Condition | Status | code |
128	|---|---|---|
129	| No route matches the method and path; unknown or foreign slug | 404 | `not_found` |
130	| Missing, malformed or unknown bearer token; bad admin key | 401 | `unauthorized` |
131	| Over the rate limit (adds a `Retry-After` header) | 429 | `rate_limited` |
132	| `Content-Length` > 8192 (the response sets `Connection: close` and the body is not read) | 413 | `payload_too_large` |
133	| Body is not valid UTF-8 JSON, or is not an object | 400 | `invalid_json` |
134	| Schema violation: missing or extra key, wrong type, bad URL, slug, `expires_in` or `now` | 400 | `invalid_request` |
135	| Slug already exists, or is reserved (`healthz`) | 409 | `slug_taken` |
136	| Link expired (E7 only) | 410 | `gone` |
137	| Unhandled exception | 500 | `internal` |
138	
139	Precedence (first failure wins): route 404 → auth 401 → rate limit 429 → size 413 → JSON 400 → validation 400 → resource state 404/409/410.
140	
141	## Acceptance criteria
142	
143	- **AC1 (R1, R15):** `serve --port 0` prints exactly the `LISTENING` line. `GET /healthz` returns 200. SIGINT (or CTRL_BREAK_EVENT on Windows) makes it exit 0 within 5 s.
144	- **AC2 (R2):** E2 with the right key returns 201 and a token matching `^lv_[0-9a-f]{32}$`. With a wrong key it returns 401. The DB holds the SHA-256 of the token, never the plaintext.
145	- **AC3 (R3):** E3, E4 and E5 without a valid bearer token return 401 `unauthorized`.
146	- **AC4 (R4, R5):** E3 without `slug` returns a slug matching `^[a-z0-9]{7}$`. A custom `slug` is echoed back. A repeated slug returns 409. `healthz` and `ab` return 409 and 400 respectively.
147	- **AC5 (R6):** `ftp://x`, `javascript:alert(1)`, `http://`, a URL with a space, and a 2049-character URL each return 400 `invalid_request`.
148	- **AC6 (R7):** `GET /<slug>` returns 302 with the exact `Location`. A later E5 shows `clicks` 1 and `last_clicked_at` set to now.
149	- **AC7 (R8, R12):** With the fake clock at T and `expires_in=60`, the link resolves 302 at T+59 and 410 at T+60. Its clicks stay at the T+59 value.
150	- **AC8 (R9, R10):** Token B gets 404 on E5 and E6 for token A's slug. A's E4 lists only A's links in order. After E6, `GET /<slug>` returns 404 and the slug can be created again.
151	- **AC9 (R11):** With `--rate-limit 3` and the fake clock at a window start plus 10 s, requests 1-3 succeed. Request 4 returns 429 with `Retry-After: 50`. After the clock moves to the next window, the next request succeeds. Redirects are never limited.
152	- **AC10 (R13):** After a restart on the same DB, tokens still authenticate, and links and clicks are unchanged.
153	- **AC11 (R14):** 50 concurrent `GET /<slug>` requests leave `clicks == 50`.
154	- **AC12 (R16):** `shorten` prints the link JSON and exits 0. A 409 makes it exit 1 with empty stdout. An unreachable server makes it exit 3. A missing token makes it exit 2.

24

Non-goals: external deployment, production Internet exposure, TLS, UI, token revocation, migrations beyond exact version-1 schema, extra runtime libraries, alternate endpoints or inferred URL restrictions. 27	## 4. Architecture
28	
29	Use `linkvault/__init__.py`, `__main__.py` and small storage/core, server and client modules. One `ThreadingHTTPServer` binds `127.0.0.1`; one SQLite connection with `check_same_thread=False` is protected by an application lock. Complete storage operations, including redirect lookup/expiry/update/commit, are serialized; do not hold storage locks during network I/O. In-memory clock/rate state is synchronized. The CLI uses argparse and urllib. [C: R14; Research B/C; S1–S4]
30	
31	A single response helper ensures compact ASCII JSON, UTF-8 bytes, listed key order and byte-correct Content-Length. Empty 204/302 bodies have length zero. Link JSON derives short_url from the actual bound port, not persistent data. [C: Conventions, E6/E7]

33	## 5. Detailed Design
34	
35	### HTTP pipeline and routes
36	
37	Implement precisely E1–E8 from the contract: health, admin token issue, authenticated link create/list/inspect/delete, public redirect, and fake-clock-only admin update. Strip query strings only; do not normalize trailing slashes or decode paths. All unlisted method/path pairs return JSON 404, including unsupported methods. Malformed slug path parameters fail route matching before auth. Preserve the original request target where stdlib normalizes leading slashes. [C: Endpoints, Error handling; S1]
38	
39	First failure wins: route → auth → rate limit → size → JSON → validation → resource state. Apply the universal 8192-byte maximum after route/auth/quota, even on ignored-body endpoints; ignored bodies do not undergo JSON/schema validation. Oversize returns 413, Connection: close, without reading the body. Missing Content-Length means empty. Decode explicitly as UTF-8 and reject non-object JSON as invalid_json. Object schema violations are invalid_request. [C: Conventions, Error handling; Research B; S1/S5]
40	
41	### Auth, validation and ownership
42	
43	Admin routes require the configured nonempty X-Admin-Key. Generate tokens as `lv_` plus `secrets.token_hex(16)`; persist only SHA-256 hex digest of the complete token. All links routes require a known bearer token. Ownership checks filter by digest; foreign links return 404. [C: R2/R3/R9]
44	
45	Custom slugs use full-match ASCII `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{3,32}`; case matters. Validate shape before checking the reserved `healthz` or global uniqueness (409). Generated slugs use exactly seven `secrets.choice` draws from lowercase letters/digits; retry at most five allocations and return 500 on exhaustion. Delete frees the slug. Optional null slug/expiry is invalid; expiry is an exact int (not bool), 1–31536000. No extra create keys. [C: R4/R5, E3]
46	
47	Validate original URL before parsing: str, <=2048 characters, no whitespace, no codepoint below 0x21 or equal to 0x7F; catch urlsplit failures; require case-insensitive http/https and nonempty hostname. Do not validate ports or normalize/rewrite accepted URLs. [C: R6; S6]
48	
49	### Time, quota and persistence
50	
51	Use integer epoch seconds (floor of wall-clock time). ISO inputs require exact ASCII `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` shape and valid UTC calendar fields. Use UTC epoch arithmetic for portability. Fake time accepts backward moves, is frozen and is not persisted. Snapshot now once per logical operation. [C: R8/R11/R12; S7]
